findings.quote: My bike was stolen in June. I bought a new bike
findings.note: The word 'bike' recurs in consecutive sentences; the first occurrence is in 'My bike was stolen in June.'
Stock phrase that delays the content.

findings.quote: The decision to sell was made
findings.note: The noun "decision" buries the verb "decide" within the weak passive "was made".
The noun "evaluation" buries the verb "evaluate" within the weak phrasal verb "carried out".
The noun "realization" buries the verb "realize"; the clause is carried by the weak phrase "come to."

findings.quote: straitjacket that ties every team to the same Thursday
findings.note: Mixed figure: 'safety net' and 'straitjacket' are two images that cannot both hold, and the literal claim behind the second is left unsaid.
"Clearly" claims obviousness the paragraph has not yet shown.
"review" is the noun; "conduct" is an empty verb burying the action of reviewing.
"determination" is a nominalization of "determine," buried under the empty verb "makes."

findings.quote: The board then posts its decisions
findings.note: Sentence template: three consecutive sentences open with "The board" ("The board meets", "The board makes", "The board then posts").

findings.quote: A change finished on a Friday therefore waits six days.
findings.note: The link to the previous sentence (which was about posting decisions) arrives only at the end, in 'therefore waits six days'. The sentence opens on 'A change finished on a Friday', which the prior sequence about the board's schedule did not introduce.

findings.quote: Concerns have been raised about the delays for over a year.
findings.note: The draft never says who raised the concerns or when exactly they raised them.
Opens on gluten development, a general baking fact, where the previous sentence was about Tom driving to the cash-and-carry for flour.
Stock image standing in for the argument; the draft leaves unsaid what the street was meant to be alerted to and by whom.
The noun "decision" buries the verb "decide" in a phrase carried by the empty verb "made".
Nominalization: "decide" is buried as a noun under an empty "be" verb.
Nominalization: "conduct" is buried under a passive "be" verb.
The noun expectation buries the verb expect, carried by the weak construction there was.
The noun observation buries the verb observe, carried by the weak verb made.

findings.quote: It is a feeling that recurs.
findings.note: Restatement: repeats the point already made by "It is a feeling that is familiar."
Passive with no actor named; the draft never says who would make the decision.
The draft never says who tabled the matter.
